name: Shishak
title: Egyptian pharaoh who invaded Judah
summary: Shishak (also known as Shoshenq I) was an Egyptian pharaoh from the 22nd dynasty who invaded the kingdom of Judah during the reign of King Rehoboam. He plundered the temple and the royal palace in Jerusalem, taking with him treasures, including the golden shields that Solomon had made. His invasion is seen as a tool of God to discipline Judah because of their unfaithfulness.

keyEvents.title: Jeroboam flees to Egypt
keyEvents.description: Jeroboam fled to Shishak in Egypt to escape King Solomon's anger and remained there until Solomon died.

keyEvents.title: Shishak's invasion of Judah
keyEvents.description: In the fifth year of Rehoboam's reign, Shishak marched against Jerusalem with a vast army, including 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen.

keyEvents.title: The prophet Shemaiah warns Rehoboam
keyEvents.description: The prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah and explained that Shishak's invasion was the Lord's punishment because they had abandoned Him.

keyEvents.title: Judah humbles himself before the Lord
keyEvents.description: When Rehoboam and the leaders humbled themselves, the Lord's anger turned away, but they still became servants of Shishak to learn the difference between serving the Lord and serving foreign kings.

keyEvents.title: Plundering of the temple and the royal palace
keyEvents.description: Shishak took the treasures from the house of the Lord and the king's house, including all the gold shields that Solomon had made. Rehoboam replaced them with bronze shields.

keyEvents.title: Shishak's campaign documented at Karnak
keyEvents.description: Shishak's military campaign against cities in both Judah and Israel is mentioned as part of his conquests and is confirmed by historical sources outside the Bible.
